title: The Evening Brief: Playoffs arrive, injuries mount across four sports
dek: Monday brought the MLB postseason to life and injury cascades across the NFL and college football, while the WNBA's No. 8 seed stunned the top seed and an American cyclist ended a 33-year medal drought.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The calendar turned toward October with playoff fields set and seasons shifting, but injuries to star position players and quarterbacks reshaped depth charts and timelines across football.
bottom_line: The MLB playoffs begin tomorrow with 12 teams set after September's final day, while the NFL and college football absorbed cascading injuries to starting quarterbacks and a star running back, forcing depth-chart reshuffles mid-season. Porzingis remains sidelined as the Warriors begin training camp, and Stewart's dominant Game 1 performance gave the Liberty a shot at historic upset. The coming days will test whether injured backup quarterbacks and fill-in running backs can stabilize struggling rosters, whether Moore can clear concussion protocol, and whether the Liberty can finish off the Lynx on Tuesday.
body: The 2026 MLB playoff field is complete. The Astros secured the AL West when the Rangers fell 6-4 to the Twins on the same day. The Wild Card Series begin Tuesday, September 29. The Phillies' path to safety came after an offensive awakening: they scored just three runs in their four-game losing streak but broke through with early runs against Tampa Bay, with Kyle Schwarber doubling home two runs in the second inning and Bryce Harper adding a solo homer in the fifth. Zack Wheeler took the mound on short rest and allowed one run over six innings. Jesús Luzardo, sidelined since September 7 with left shoulder inflammation, made his first appearance against hitters in the eighth and retired the side on four pitches, signaling readiness for the postseason ahead.

Football's injury toll accelerated across three fronts. Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane tore his ACL in the first quarter of the Week 3 loss to Kansas City and is out for the season. The non-contact injury occurred when Achane planted his left leg to cut right, and the leg gave out beneath him. The Dolphins will rely on Ollie Gordon II, who carries 90 career carries into full-time duty. Tampa Bay's Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb on his throwing hand late in Sunday's 23-16 loss to Minnesota and is expected to miss three weeks. An MRI revealed no fracture or ligament damage. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will start against Green Bay on October 5, with Mayfield eligible to return October 25 against Carolina. The Buccaneers are 0-3 and face Green Bay, Dallas, and Pittsburgh in their next three games. The New York Giants acquired quarterback JJ McCarthy from Minnesota for a 2027 fifth-round pick after starter Jaxson Dart underwent season-ending knee surgery. Jameis Winston starts Sunday against Arizona. McCarthy, a 23-year-old who played under Jim Harbaugh at Michigan, was the 10th pick in the 2024 draft but fell behind Kyler Murray on Minnesota's depth chart. In 10 career starts, he has thrown 12 interceptions against 11 touchdowns and ranked last among qualified quarterbacks in completion percentage (58%), passer rating (72.6), and touchdown-to-interception ratio.

College football's injury cascade touched Oregon. Quarterback Dante Moore sustained a concussion in the second quarter of Saturday's 41-27 win over USC after being hit by linebacker Desman Stephens. MRI and CT scans came back clean, but Moore enters concussion protocol with no timetable for return. Stephens was penalized for targeting and ejected, then suspended for USC's October 3 game against Washington for his conduct after the hit. Stephens released a statement calling his reaction "completely inappropriate and inexcusable." Backup Dylan Raiola, a former Nebraska starter, led Oregon to victory and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in Moore's absence. The Ducks enter a bye week before hosting UCLA on October 10.

The WNBA's first-round playoffs delivered an upset. The No. 8 seed New York Liberty defeated the No. 1 seed Minnesota Lynx 91-75 on September 27 in Game 1 of their best-of-three series. Breanna Stewart scored 34 points and grabbed 12 rebounds, shooting 11 of 18 from the field and adding 6 assists, 2 steals, and 2 blocks. Stewart's performance marked her third career 30-point, 10-rebound playoff game, second only to A'ja Wilson all time. The Liberty host Game 2 on Tuesday with a chance to become the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in WNBA history.

Brandon McNulty won the UCI world road race championship in Montreal on September 27, becoming the first American man to claim the title in 33 years since Lance Armstrong in Oslo in 1993. The 28-year-old time-trialist and domestique completed the 273.4-kilometer course in 6 hours 17 minutes, finishing 13 seconds ahead of Michael Matthews of Australia. McNulty's win came as an upset; Tadej Pogacar, cycling's strongest rider, did not start due to injury, and Mathieu van der Poel finished third.

The Golden State Warriors open training camp with center Kristaps Porzingis unavailable. The 31-year-old, acquired from Atlanta in February and signed to a two-year, $40 million extension, is sidelined indefinitely with an undisclosed health issue. GM Mike Dunleavy said he is not marking Porzingis out for the season start, though Porzingis missed 16 of 31 games after the trade deadline and has not played more than 60 games in the last four seasons. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, the No. 11 pick in the 2026 draft, will assume a larger role in Porzingis's absence.

Jonathan Greenard made his Philadelphia Eagles debut against Chicago on Monday night after clearing a pectoral injury sustained over the summer. The edge rusher missed all of training camp and the first two regular-season games. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio cautioned that Greenard is not ready for a full workload. The Eagles' pass rush has generated 45% pressure through two games but totaled only three sacks.
